chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Salih ibn Razin and Muhammad ibn Marwan and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Every eye will be weeping on the Day of Judgment except for three: an eye that was closed from the prohibitions of Allah, an eye that stayed awake in obedience to Allah, and an eye that wept in the depth of the night from the fear of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of eyes that will not weep on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the physical manifestation of spiritual states on the Day of Judgment, where the 'weeping' of the eyes signifies either regret or divine joy. This hadith categorizes the eyes into three distinct types: those that guarded against sin, those that dedicated their vigilance to worship, and those moved by khushu' (humility) during night prayers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of action and inner consciousness. The 'weeping' here is not merely sorrow but a testament to the eye's role as a witness to one's deeds, distinguishing the righteous who will weep tears of relief from the wicked who weep in despair.
